cues.en: Now last but not least, let me show one
totally optional optimization or restructuring in the code.
Right now I access the DOM here in show tooltip when I append my tooltip container and in hide tooltip
when I remove it and there is nothing wrong with it and for a web component as simple as this one,
this might actually be the best way of doing it but it's also worth looking at a pattern which you see
from time to time and which I at least want to get you thinking about,
you can add a method in your class as we did it before,
let's say we call it _render, the name is totally up to you though. It's not a reserved name,
I just want to make sure it's private
to really make clear that we only call it from inside this class and I name it render because this should
be a method which is responsible for updating the DOM.
So what I now will do is I will go up to my constructor and add a new property,
this _tooltipVisible and I'll set it to false initially,
so initially this should not be visible.
Now of course we're not using this property yet,
I want to use that in the render method now.
Here I'll check if this tooltip visible is true and if it is true, then I want to create and append
this element.
So here I'll go there,
copy that code and append this child, else
I will execute the code for removing the child, let me grab that and paste it in there. This also
means that the tooltip container now can be converted back to a constant that only exists in the
render method because I don't access it anywhere else.
So I can go up there,
remove the tooltip container in my constructor and in the render method, I'll simply add a new variable
with let tooltip container and I'll then simply initialize it here, set its text content here and add it
here in the end or remove it
here. For this I'll just check if tooltip container is defined and I'll only try to remove it if it is
defined, otherwise
if this was undefined still and we somehow would end up here, we would face a problem.
Now with the render method defined in show tooltip, all I have to do is I have to switch to tooltip visible
property to true, excuse me and then execute the render method again because in there, I
will then have all the logic for checking tooltip visible and adding the container and in hide tooltip,
I'll do the opposite,
I'll set tooltip visible to false and then execute the render method.
Now what's the idea behind this approach?
Well the more and more logic you add, maybe you also render other things in your component at some
point of time, the more sense it makes to do all that rendering in a central place, so that you quickly
can have a look at all your rendering related code in one place instead of having different parts of
rendering different parts of your DOM distributed throughout your component, instead
now we know in the render method, we have all the logic for accessing our shadow DOM and for adding our
tooltip container in this case
but if we had any other things we wanted to render, we would do it in there too
and so we could always quickly see what we're doing with our DOM in our component and all the other
places and all the other methods of our component are only responsible for updating data, which is then
getting used in render to update the DOM correctly,
like we're using tooltip visible to update the DOM correctly by either adding or removing our tooltip container
and we're only setting the data here and then of course we always have to call render when we know that
we changed something that should trigger a re-render. We can also call render initially here, even though
we don't require it for this component
but we can call it initially here in the connected callback to say hey when this component gets loaded
for the first time, we also want to render it for the first time.
Now if I reload here, this of course has no special effect because we don't show the tooltip because
initially we have the tooltip visible status set to false but we do render it as soon as I hover over
this,
now it's not getting removed anymore if I hover away,
let me quickly check that, yes this makes sense,
this check here and also the way we removed this will not work, tooltip container always gets re-initialized
to an empty, to an undefined variable when render gets called, the old state is of course not carried
over
so this will not be set
if we call render after changing tooltip visible to false.
So what I should do instead is I should initialize this with my loaded tooltip container
if available, so I will simply access my shadow root here and there,
I'll query for either a div because I know my tooltip container will be the only div or of course
we could also assign a class to our tooltip container to query by that or an ID
but here I'll do it by this
and now if this is set, then I can remove it and I do load it whenever render is called.
So with this change in place, if I now reload this, still everything works,
no errors here,
if I hover over this get shown, I can hover away and this now all works with this central render method.
Again, not something we need so much for this trivial component
but the more complex your components get, the more different parts of your shadow
DOM you might be updating, the more sense it makes to do all this updating in one central place where
you can then quickly see all your updating logic instead of having it distributed across your entire
component and all the methods in your component.
